# Review: `fix(sync): a server counter past the last event no longer pulls the run every two seconds` (dc4a7ed)

Worktree `C:\Users\xbox\ScrtGit\sbm-ui\.worktrees\the-run-stops-re-pulling`. The commit touches 6 files (91/0, 21/1, 6/1, 73/0, 43/7, 13/0). Note on the artifact: the branch's parent is `4c56f34`, one commit behind `origin/main` (`e0561fd`, deck profiles #308), so `review-e0561fd..dc4a7ed.diff` shows 16 files of streamdeck/deck-profiles "deletions" that are not in the commit at all. I reviewed `git show dc4a7ed` instead.

## Root cause confirmed: yes, all three

Pre-fix, from `git show origin/main:apps/web/src/sync/engine.ts`:

- **Refetch every pass.** `:133` `const before = tailSeq(stamped)` and `:183` `if (serverTail > before + incoming.length)`. `serverTail` is `theirs?.seq` (the session counter). With the counter at 8 and the log's tail at 7 the test is `8 > 7 + 0` on every pass forever, since nothing carried the fact that the gap had already been looked at.
- **`aboutTheRun` true by identity.** `:210` `members !== local.members`. `client.ts:769-777` parses fresh JSON per call, so `got.members` is a new array every time, while `asks` on `:213` was already compared by value.
- **`useRun` clearing `pending` on every `pulled`.** `apps/web/src/run/useRun.ts:267-275` pre-fix: `currentRun(pack.id).then((saved) => { ... setEvents(saved.events); ... setPending(null); })`, unconditional.

Corroboration that the gap is legitimate and permanent: the session counter is `UpdateExpression: "ADD seq :n"` on the META row (`hosted/infra/lib/handlers/store.ts:798-806`), so it is monotonic and numbers reserved by a transaction that then fails as a repeat are burned; `eventsAfter` (`store.ts:754-773`) pages the whole range with no cap, so a short answer means the events genuinely do not exist.

One correction to the brief, which the report already makes: `db.saveRun` is `storage/db.ts:464`, a plain `put` that emits nothing. The two-second cadence comes from `run/store.ts:50`. The loop needed a local write each turn; what made it a loop is that the pass was guaranteed to drop the block in flight, so the player moved again and handed it the next `localChange`.

## Case analysis

The invariant the fix rests on: `seq` now means "everything numbered at or below this is either in my log or known not to exist on the server", and the fetch still asks `after: before` (the log's own tail, `engine.ts:197`), never `after: seenTail`. So an advance of `seq` never moves the fetch cursor.

**(a) Another device appends past this device's seenTail.** Its event takes counter+1, which is strictly greater than any `serverTail` this device has persisted (the counter only ever adds). The manifest's pointer seq moves (`store.ts:652-666`, written by `touchPointers`), so `serverTail > seenTail + 0` and the fetch fires, from `before` — so the new event and anything in the gap region come back together. Fetched, not skipped.

**(b) Pending events with the server ahead.** `appendEvents` sets `serverTail = max(manifest, sent.seq)` (`engine.ts:188`) and `incoming = sent.appended`. If the only new numbers are my own, `serverTail == seenTail + incoming.length` and no fetch is needed. If another device slipped an event in between, `sent.seq` exceeds `seenTail + incoming.length` and the fetch fires. Duplicate-suppressed appends (the SEEN path, `store.ts:820-843`) return a short `appended` with the full tail in `seq`, which makes the test more likely to fire, never less. Correct in both directions.

**(c) First pass on an older record whose `seq` equals the log tail.** `seenTail = max(before, local.seq) = before`, so the gate is identical to the pre-fix one and the first pass behaves exactly as before: it fetches, sees nothing behind the gap, and only then writes the higher `seq`. Old records are forward-compatible, and the first advance always follows a fetch that answered.

**(d) The live case, three passes.** Pass 1: `seenTail` 7, `serverTail` 8, fetch `after=7`, no events, fresh members that now compare equal by value, so `aboutTheRun` is false; `caughtUp = max(7, 8) = 8 ≠ local.seq`, so the record is saved with `seq: 8` and nothing is pushed to `pulledRuns`; `syncBus.pulled` drops an empty list (`sync/bus.ts:37`), so the page hears nothing and the roll survives. Pass 2: `seenTail = 8`, `serverTail = 8`, no fetch, `caughtUp === local.seq`, `changed` false, no write, no news. Pass 3: identical to pass 2. The pass is inert, which is what makes the schedule stop mattering. This is exactly what the new engine test asserts, including `getSession r1 after 2` on the first pass and no `getSession` at all on the second.

**(e) `!theirs`.** `serverTail` stays 0, so `caughtUp = tailSeq(merged)` from whatever the server numbered in `createSession` or the full `getSession(id, 0)`. This can lower a record's `seq`, and that is the right answer: a session recreated from scratch starts its counter again, and carrying the old high-water mark forward would suppress real fetches. The cost is one extra catch-up pass for a run the manifest stopped listing; no correctness issue.

**Is there a path where a real remote event is skipped because `seq` was persisted past it?** One, and it is not currently reachable with events behind it. At `engine.ts:196-204` the fetch is attempted but `got` is null, and `caughtUp` at `:237` is still `max(tailSeq(merged), serverTail)` — the device records itself caught up to a counter it never read behind. `api.getSession` returns null only for a non-200 JSON answer or `found: false` (`client.ts:769-777`); `>=500` throws `SyncError` and is caught at `engine.ts:263-266` with no save, and the session route answers `200 {found:false}` only when the session rows are gone or this account is not a member (`hosted/infra/lib/handlers/api.ts:2569-2575`), i.e. when there is nothing left to fetch. So no live event loss. It also self-heals: because the fetch cursor is `before`, the next time the counter moves the missed range comes back. Still worth closing (see Issues).
